story_title: Breakfast in Mexico City, lunch in Brickell
story: For many families in Mexico City, Miami is a second home. The bank is in Brickell, the apartment overlooks Biscayne Bay, the kids know the beach at Key Biscayne better than any in Mexico. Getting there used to mean a morning flight out of the capital's main airport, a long immigration line at MIA and an hour in traffic on the Dolphin Expressway. A private jet to Miami trims all of that down to a quiet morning and a nonstop flight across the Gulf of Mexico.

You land at Opa-locka Executive, north of downtown, and clear US Customs inside the private terminal in minutes. Twenty minutes later you are crossing the causeway to South Beach, windows down, the water a shade of green that never looks real in photographs. By early afternoon you can be at lunch in the Design District or on a lounger in Mid-Beach. On Sunday, the same aircraft flies you home, and Monday starts in Mexico City as planned.
why_title: Why book your private jet to Miami with JETCAB

why.d: JETCAB flies from Toluca to Miami-Opa Locka Executive in about 3 hours 30 minutes nonstop. There is no connection through Dallas or Houston and no gate change, so the whole family stays together from the car door to the beach.

US Customs and Border Protection clears you inside the private terminal at Opa-locka, usually in minutes. JETCAB files the eAPIS manifest about 24 hours before departure, so officers already have your details when the aircraft door opens.

A Learjet 35 for up to 7 passengers starts at $4,800 USD one way, a Challenger 605 for 12 at $9,500 and a Gulfstream GV for 16 at $18,000. Crew, fuel, catering and permits are always included in the quote.

JETCAB has flown from Toluca since 1999 under an operating permit from the AFAC, Mexico's civil aviation authority. Send your dates on WhatsApp and a confirmed price for your private jet to Miami arrives within 30 minutes.

journey_title: From Mexico City to South Beach in a single morning

journey.d: Your driver heads west to Toluca International Airport, 45 to 60 minutes by car from Polanco, Lomas or Santa Fe. On a busy morning, a helicopter transfer covers the same distance in about 25 minutes and lands you right at the airport.

Passports are checked at the private terminal while your bags go straight to the aircraft. You walk from the car to the aircraft steps in under 10 minutes, with the eAPIS manifest already filed the day before.

The route heads northeast over Veracruz and out across the Gulf of Mexico. Breakfast is served on board, and the cabin is private, so you can sleep, work or simply watch the water turn from deep blue to turquoise.

About 3 hours 30 minutes after takeoff, you land at Miami-Opa Locka Executive. Miami runs one or two hours ahead of Mexico City, depending on the season. Customs takes minutes inside the FBO, and your car waits outside.

Twenty minutes later you are crossing Biscayne Bay to South Beach, or 25 minutes south to Brickell. Drop your bags, change into something lighter, and walk out to lunch while the afternoon is still young.

places_title: What to do in Miami after your private jet lands

places.name: South Beach
places.d: The Art Deco Historic District along Ocean Drive and Collins Avenue holds hundreds of pastel buildings from the 1930s and 1940s. Mornings are for the wide sand at Lummus Park, afternoons for the pool, and evenings for dinner on Collins as the neon signs come on.

places.name: Brickell
places.d: Miami's financial district, just south of the Miami River, packs international banks, residential towers and restaurants into a few walkable blocks. Brickell City Centre has shops and dining under an open-air canopy, and the causeway to Key Biscayne and its quiet beaches starts a few minutes away.

places.name: Wynwood
places.d: A former warehouse district north of downtown, Wynwood is now known for some of the most photographed street art in the United States. The Wynwood Walls, opened in 2009, anchor the neighborhood, with galleries, breweries and good restaurants filling the blocks around them.

places.name: Miami Design District
places.d: A compact neighborhood of flagship stores from houses such as Hermès, Dior and Louis Vuitton, with architecture and public art at every corner. The Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami is free to visit, and Buckminster Fuller's Fly's Eye Dome sits in Palm Court.

best_time_title: Best time to fly private to Miami
best_time: Miami's high season runs from December to April, when the air is dry, the sea is calm and daytime temperatures sit in the mid to upper 70s Fahrenheit. It is also when the city fills up. Art Basel Miami Beach takes over the first week of December, the Miami Open tennis tournament arrives in March, and the Formula 1 Miami Grand Prix brings huge crowds in May. Stone crab season runs from October 15 to May 1. Hurricane season lasts from June 1 to November 30, with afternoon storms most summer days. For holiday weeks and event weekends, book your aircraft and hotel well ahead.
airport_title: Miami-Opa Locka Executive (OPF): arriving in Miami
airport: JETCAB flies to Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport (OPF), north of downtown Miami. It is about 20 minutes from South Beach and 25 minutes from Brickell, and it serves private and corporate aircraft away from the crowds at Miami International. US Customs and Border Protection clears international arrivals inside the FBO, usually within minutes, using the eAPIS manifest JETCAB files about 24 hours before departure. Your bags stay with the aircraft until they go into your car, and your driver can wait just outside the private terminal.
docs_title: Documents for a private flight to Miami
docs: Every passenger needs a valid passport, and Mexican citizens also need a valid US visa. Travelers of other nationalities need the entry document their passport requires for the United States. JETCAB files the eAPIS manifest with US Customs and Border Protection, so we need passenger names, dates of birth and passport details about 24 hours before departure. Officers check documents at the FBO when you land.

faq.q: How long is a private jet flight from Mexico City to Miami?
faq.a: About 3 hours 30 minutes nonstop from Toluca International Airport (TLC) to Miami-Opa Locka Executive (OPF). Add 45 to 60 minutes by car from Polanco, Santa Fe, Lomas or Interlomas to Toluca, or about 25 by helicopter, and roughly 20 minutes from Opa-locka to South Beach.

faq.q: How much does a private jet to Miami cost?
faq.a: From Mexico City, a private jet to Miami starts at $4,800 USD one way on a Learjet 35 for up to 7 passengers, $9,500 on a Challenger 605 for 12 and $18,000 on a Gulfstream GV for 16. Prices are per aircraft and include crew, fuel, catering and permits.

faq.q: Is Miami Executive Airport for private jets?
faq.a: Yes. Miami Executive Airport (TMB), in Kendall, southwest of the city, is a general aviation airport used by private aircraft. For flights from Mexico City, JETCAB lands at Miami-Opa Locka Executive (OPF), north of downtown, where US Customs clears passengers inside the FBO and South Beach is about 20 minutes away.

faq.q: What documents do I need to fly private to Miami?
faq.a: A valid passport for every passenger and, for Mexican citizens, a valid US visa. JETCAB needs passenger details about 24 hours before departure to file the eAPIS manifest with US Customs. Officers check your documents inside the private terminal at Opa-locka when you land.

faq.q: Do you tip a private jet pilot?
faq.a: Tipping is not expected, because crew costs are already part of the charter price. If the pilots and crew made the trip especially easy, a thank-you note or a gratuity handed to the captain is a kind gesture. It is always optional, and nobody will expect it.

faq.q: What is the cheapest way to fly private to Miami?
faq.a: The Learjet 35 is the most affordable option at $4,800 USD one way for up to 7 passengers, which comes to under $700 per seat with a full cabin. Since you pay for the whole aircraft, flying with family or colleagues is the easiest way to bring the cost per person down.
